lesson_title: Demand, Supply and the Outbreak That Moved Egg Prices
hook_text: Bird flu hits the farms. Egg prices climb in weeks. Nobody decided that. So who did?
clip_script: Apply this to the outbreak. Ask the two diagnostic questions every market answer needs. First: which side of the market was struck — buyers or sellers? The disease hit the farms, so the supply side. Second: did the price of eggs cause the change? No — a virus did. Therefore we shift the whole supply curve rather than sliding along it. Direction? With millions of hens culled, farmers can offer fewer eggs at every conceivable price: the supply curve shifts leftward. The diagnosis is complete: demand curve untouched, supply curve shifted left — and that piece of reasoning carries a large share of the marks in any market question.
visual_style: News-style shots of empty egg shelves cutting to a clean animated market diagram: the supply curve sliding left, the equilibrium dot climbing to a higher price.
mood: Urgent and topical, resolving into calm logic.
pacing: Fast hook, steady two-question method, sharp landing on the shifted curve.
